note: Re-judged by an independent judge after the row's annotation moved from {not-applicable} to {gap}. RFC 9012 Section 3.2.5 reads 'Unless a key value is being advertised, the MPLS-in-GRE Encapsulation sub-TLV MUST NOT be present.' The party that decides whether the sub-TLV is present is the BGP speaker originating the Tunnel Encapsulation attribute, Ze's declared role, and Ze already originates the attribute for SR Policy. MPLS-in-GRE (tunnel type 11) is an absent feature, not a role Ze does not fill, and no owner decision declines it, so the earlier not-applicable verdict no longer stands and the row is a conformance gap. Ze builds no MPLS-in-GRE Encapsulation sub-TLV: internal/component/bgp/plugins/nlri/srpolicy/config.go::buildTunnelEncap writes tunnel type 15 with the RFC 9830 sub-TLVs only. An operator can originate a type 11 Tunnel TLV as a generic attribute 0x17: internal/component/bgp/textparse/rawattr.go::decodeTypedRawAttribute returns the opaque form for a code no keyword names, so an MPLS-in-GRE Encapsulation sub-TLV with no key goes out unrefused.
